subject: Order Form handoff + pen-test scheduling for SOC2 evidence (Acme Medical)
messages:
From: Mira Patel <mira.patel@acme-med.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-med.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form draft + security exhibit questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the draft order form — the commercial terms look good. Before we loop in legal, two quick asks from our security and procurement teams: 

1) Can you confirm Redwood's SOC 2 report date and whether it includes coverage for hosting regions in us-west-2?
2) We need clarity on the "penetration testing" clause in the security exhibit: specifically whether Acme can schedule an annual external pen test against a staging environment and the expected notice period (we typically require 30 days).
3) Evidence cadence: our auditors want a point-of-contact and an expected turnaround for artifact requests (logs, config screenshots, scoped procedures).

I've attached our standard procurement checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Mira
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Medical Systems
Attachments: Acme_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Mira Patel <mira.patel@acme-med.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft + security exhibit questions

Hi Mira — appreciate the quick review. Short answers up front: 

- SOC 2: Latest report dated 2027-01 covering production and our hosted regions including us-west-2. We can share the full report under NDA; I attached the Redwood SOC2 cover PDF for now.
- Pen test: Redwood supports annual external pen tests against a staging environment. Standard notice: 14 days for typical windows; we can accommodate 30 days if you prefer. There are a few gating items (ephemeral creds, scope checklist) that we coordinate with ops.
- Evidence cadence: We nominate a single evidence owner on our side and aim for 3 business days for non-sensitive artifact requests and 10 business days for operational playbooks/checklists. Exceptions for legal discovery or large dataset exports.

I'll loop in Laura (legal) and Monica (security/trust) to confirm contractual language and any coverage carve-outs. Also attaching the latest draft of the order form with our baseline security exhibit inserted — see filename Redwood_OrderForm_Acme_v3.docx.

Next steps: Laura and Monica, can you confirm whether the attached wording needs redlines for the pen-test clause and if the evidence turnaround above is legally/operationally acceptable?

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_Acme_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document); SOC2-Report-2027-01.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Order form draft + security exhibit questions

Forwarding to kick off legal review. Initial read: order form looks standard; security exhibit has a few items to tighten:

- Pen-test clause: we should avoid language that implies unlimited inspection rights on production. Recommend scope be "staging environment only, with mutually agreed scope and test plan". Include required acknowledgements around no-privilege escalation of customer data.
- Notice period: 30 days is fine; propose we add a clause requiring a pre-test checklist and that Redwood reserves right to postpone for active incident windows.
- Evidence cadence: legal wants to avoid hard SLAs for evidence that could include third-party logs; recommend phrasing "reasonable efforts" plus target turnaround times for standard artifacts.

I'll prepare tracked redlines and propose a short canary clause for emergency/regulatory requests (escalation path to Redwood security with a documented SLA).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference Legal

Subject: Re: Order form draft + security exhibit questions

Hi all,

Operational notes from security: 

- Staging: We'll provide a replicated staging environment for the pen test, sanitized of production PHI/PII. Pen tests against production are not permitted.
- Scope and whitelist: Acme must provide a signed test plan. Red lines: no social engineering of Redwood staff, no attempt to exfiltrate customer data.
- Windows: we can support a 7-day testing window (daily 09:00-17:00 PDT) during a mutually agreed 30-day notice period; if Acme requests a one-off weekend run, we'll evaluate on a case-by-case basis.
- Evidence turnaround: for logs and config exports we target 3 business days; for architecture diagrams/playbooks it's 10 business days. If a request requires additional engineering time (e.g., rehydrating logs), we'll flag expected lead time up front.

I'll attach the security checklist we use for pen-tests and the staging provisioning playbook.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Head of Trust & Security Operations
Attachments: Redwood_Pentest_Checklist.pdf (application/pdf); Staging_Provisioning_Playbook.md (text/markdown)

John / Mira — attaching our proposed redlines for the security exhibit and a short "Emergency Regulatory Requests" (canary) clause for clarity. High level summary of redlines: 

- Scope: explicit "staging-only" language, required signed test plan, and bans on social engineering.
- Notice: 30-day calendar notice required; test windows defined (see Monica's note).
- Evidence: replace binding SLA language with "reasonable efforts" plus internal target turnaround times; we will include a named Redwood evidence owner and an escalation path.
- Delicacy: carve out requests that require reproducing customer data (those will require additional scoping and timeline).

I'll send the tracked Word doc (Redwood_OrderForm_Acme_v3_redlines.docx) via DocuSign/HIPAA-safe link and can accept Acme's redline packet once the SOC2 NDA is in place.

Best,
Laura Bennett
